payload.goal: Move sofar's hot path to a native Rust core without a big-bang rewrite: lock the black-box contract (SPEC plus a conformance suite over commands, hooks and record format), build sofar-core in Rust (hook handlers, event append, fold, digest/status render, statusline) behind the same CLI contract, integrate with TypeScript fallback, ship prebuilt per-platform binaries via npm, and prove it as its own benchmark arm; it ships only if no held-out lead margin shrinks (bench-refresh D19). After conformance parity, new hot-path code is Rust-only.

payload.because:
- Sofar runs on every tool call of every agent session. A native core gives near-zero hook start-up, fast folds over very large records (this repo's own is 9.7 MB), a single binary with no Node dependency for Codex/Cursor/OpenCode users, and headroom for many parallel agents.
- Measured 0.31 hooks are only ~0.75% of session time today, so the win is future scale and distribution rather than today's tokens. That is why it goes incrementally, and must pass the same benchmark gate as any other change.
- A conformance-first strangler port means neither implementation can drift from the SPEC.
payload.chose:
Adopt Rust for sofar's HOT PATH, incrementally, starting now. Ruled by the run owner 2026-09-15 ("yes do it").
SUPERSEDES, for the hot path only, the CLAUDE.md engineering conventions:
- "TypeScript strict mode; Node ≥18; ES modules";
- "Dependencies: … Nothing else without logging a Decision". Rust crates are limited to serde, serde_json and ulid until another Decision adds one.

Scope of `sofar-core`: hook handlers (session-start, user-prompt-submit, post-tool-use, stop, session-end), atomic event append, fold, digest/status render, and statusline.

TypeScript keeps: the MCP server, `sofar drive`, init/doctor/review, and cloud commands.

The contract comes first: docs/SPEC.md plus a black-box conformance suite over commands, hook stdin/stdout, env and record bytes. It runs against BOTH implementations.

The schema rail holds: event payload types stay authored ONLY in packages/schema/src. Rust types are GENERATED from them, never hand-written. Projection templates keep one source of truth, and Rust output is verified byte-identical by golden tests.

Parity gate: 100% conformance, perf targets met, and a benchmark arm "sofar-rust-core" vs "sofar-ts" that shrinks no D19 lead margin.

Sequencing: r1-fixes waves 1–2 land in TypeScript now, and the Rust core must reach parity INCLUDING them. After parity, new hot-path code is Rust-only, which stops the TypeScript port surface growing. Distribution: prebuilt per-platform binaries through npm optionalDependencies, with a TypeScript fallback.
payload.over:
- A big-bang rewrite now: it freezes waves 1–3, leaves round 2 unable to attribute gains, and means porting 27.6k engine lines and 34k test lines before anything is trustworthy.
- Staying TypeScript-only behind a measure-first gate: the run owner's point is that the port cost grows with every feature, and Codex CLI, Turborepo and Biome show the path is proven.
payload.rule: Hot-path event and projection behaviour is defined by docs/SPEC.md plus the conformance suite and must pass against both the TypeScript and Rust implementations; Rust schema types are generated from packages/schema/src, never hand-written.

plan.goal: Move sofar's hot path to a native Rust core incrementally (rust-core D1): contract first, then sofar-core in Rust behind the same CLI and hook contract, integrated with TypeScript fallback, shipped as prebuilt binaries, and proven as its own benchmark arm that shrinks no held-out lead margin (bench-refresh D19). After parity, new hot-path code is Rust-only.

payload.text:
Hook contract change from agents-parity 2.1 (D5, branch agents-parity, not yet on r1-fixes). It bears on rust-core 1.1, 2.5 and 3.1, and on memory-lead 1.4's hook mirror.

(1) Flag: every `sofar event <hook>` subcommand takes `--host codex`, in either `--host codex` or `--host=codex` form. The hot path (cli/fast.ts parseHookFlags) must accept it beside `--root`. Any other host value falls through to commander, which exits 1.

(2) Session identity: a declared Codex call registers its session as tool `codex`. Diagnostics host is `{tool:"codex"}`.

(3) Output: session-start and user-prompt stdout become `{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"SessionStart"|"UserPromptSubmit","additionalContext":<trimmed text>}}`. post-tool, stop and session-end pass through.

(4) Post-tool classification is now a list, not one call. `apply_patch` (tool_input.command holds the patch) appends one file_touched per `*** Add/Update/Delete File:` header: Add is write, Update is edit, Delete is delete. An Update followed by `*** Move to:` records delete on the source and write on the destination. Paths resolve against payload cwd. The session registers once; there is one diagnostics row per call, from the first classified subject.

(5) Codex PostToolUse fires after non-zero exits too, so command_run and file_touched omit `ok` unless tool_response reports interrupted or timed_out; the diagnostics row gets `ok:null`.

(6) Codex shims: `.codex/hooks/sofar/{session-start,user-prompt-submit,post-tool-use,stop,session-end}.sh`, each running `exec sofar event <hook> --host codex --root "$(dirname "$0")/../../.."`. `.codex/hooks.json` runs them by git-root path.

Tests: packages/engine/test/codex-host.test.ts, against test/fixtures/codex/. SPEC: §Codex host, the "Wired" paragraph.

Parity impact from drive-visibility (SPEC Driver section, 2026-09-17, decisions drive-visibility D2/D3): three rust-core surfaces gain drive liveness. (1) status render (2.4): `running` / `driver gone` / `liveness unknown` beside the latest unstopped run; (2) the user-prompt-submit hook handler (2.5): a drive line gated on a per-session last-seen id under the per-clone state dir; (3) statusline (2.6): `drive <task>` / `drive gone` / `drive <stop reason>`. All three probe `<state base>/runs/<run id>.lock` with a SHARED non-blocking flock and read HELD/FREE/ABSENT, ABSENT meaning unknown, never gone. Rust takes it with std File::try_lock_shared / try_lock (flock semantics, no new crate under rust-core D1); never fcntl/lockf. Also a new event `run_adopted {run, epoch}` for the fold (owner = highest epoch, first id on a tie). The conformance suite (1.2) should cover these once drive-visibility lands them in TypeScript.

payload.text: CI `test` job root cause (2026-09-21): every rust-core push since 3a284e6 hung in `npm test` until GitHub's 6h job limit cancelled it (runs 35201334756..35212040877; core matrix and core-conformance were green). The one file that never reported is packages/engine/test/update-check.test.ts: its 'survives a state dir it cannot write' case set XDG_STATE_HOME=/proc/definitely-not-writable, and on Linux mkdirSync({recursive:true}) under /proc gets ENOENT for the child and EEXIST for /proc and retries forever — a synchronous loop no vitest timeout can interrupt. Reproduced in Docker node:20 and node:24 (never returns); macOS throws at once, so it only shows on Linux. Fix: the unwritable state dir is a path under a regular file (ENOTDIR at once on every platform, as root too). main carries the same test but has no CI workflow, so the hang is latent there; it lands on main with the rust-core merge. Diagnosis method: vitest prints a file only when it finishes, so diff the files the CI log reported against `git ls-files '*.test.ts'` to find the one still running.

A vitest run that hangs in CI with no failure (job cancelled at the 6h limit) is a file that never finished: vitest prints a file's results only on completion, so diff the files the CI log reported against `git ls-files '*.test.ts'`. Never point a test's "unwritable" path under /proc: on Linux, mkdirSync({recursive:true}) there loops forever (ENOENT/EEXIST retry), a sync spin no test timeout can interrupt; use a path under a regular file (ENOTDIR on every platform, even as root). Reproduce Linux-only behaviour locally with Docker (`open -a Docker`, then node:20 / node:24 images).

payload.text: sofar_update_plan (plan_updated) rebuilds the phase objects, so every phase NOTE set by an earlier phase_status_changed is silently dropped. The fold warns only about task and phase STATUSES, and the plan schema has no field to restate a note. After any plan replacement, re-issue sofar_update_phase with the same status and note for each phase that had one. To write to a record that lives on another worktree's branch (e.g. rust-core in ~/IO/sofar-rust-core) from a session whose MCP server is bound to main, spawn `sofar mcp` with cwd set to that worktree and call the tools over stdio JSON-RPC (initialize, notifications/initialized, tools/call). A plan_updated from main's stale copy would clobber the branch plan on union. Event-only writes (notes, memories, session events) can instead go through main and be carried over with `sofar export <slug>` | `sofar import - <slug> --root <worktree>`, which dedupes by id.

- Fix: the parser dedupes through a key->index HashMap once an object passes a small size, and keeps JSON.parse semantics: the last value wins, at the first occurrence's position. Object::get stays linear. Behaviour is unchanged.
- PREDICTED: warm session-start at team100 from ~3.3 s to ~1.3 s (-2.0 s, ~0.4x). Cold start about -2 s of its ~7 s (~0.7x), since its tier-1 build also parses. MIRROR OWED at the next RC re-pin: drive-visibility 2.2 (be4ce88, on main after rc.2) changed the fold. Reported by peer sofar-1b on 2026-09-22; the reasoning is in drive-visibility D8 and its 2.2 task note.
- New event `run_adopted {run, epoch}`. The validator rejects epoch < 2 (run_started is epoch 1). An adoption for a run that never started is skipped with the warning `adoption of run "<id>" that never started — skipped`.
- RunState gains `adoptions: [{id, ts, epoch}]` in replay order, and `owner: {id, epoch}`. The owner starts as run_started's own event id at epoch 1. Only a STRICTLY higher epoch takes it; replay is in id order, so on a tie the first id keeps it.
- `stop_requests` now holds EVENT IDS instead of envelope timestamps; the property name is unchanged.
- run_adopted is excluded from drift, like the other driver events (record_freshness's driver list).
- Fold-parity: new case FP-11-run-adoption-fencing. The FP-06 golden and schema-fingerprint.txt are regenerated. SCHEMA_VERSION is unchanged. D21: never rename the new case id.
- describeRun, if the core renders it: `, resumed (epoch N)` after the policy once owner.epoch > 1, and "stop requested" counts only requests whose id sorts after owner.id.
- Together with typed-judge 4.1/5.1 (note 01M341T4), this is the rc.3 re-pin's scope so far. Until then the core matches rc.2, and the stub must not dispatch it under a newer engine.
